At times the stars are at their farthest points, at times their nearest; they also appear to move backwards, pause, or move forward, and they occupy their own stations, where they are said to be at home, in decline, exalted, or fallen. Their positions also depend on whether the constellations they enter are fixed, changing, or two-bodied, and on other conditions described in outline in books of astrology. Only God, exalted be His name, and His angels brought near to Him—the intellectual lights and divine rays—know all their details.

Have you not considered the kingdom of the heavens, the spirits of the spheres, and the souls of the stars: how their being is sustained, their light shines, they obey their Maker, and they keep moving without rest, out of love and longing for Him? Consider, too, the wonders of wisdom and the subtlety of care in the arrangement of the elements. Earth is at the center of all things, where its density and darkness suit its distance from the source of light. If it were beside the heavenly bodies, it would burn from the heat of their constant motion. And even if it remained there, no animal could live on it and no plant could grow from it. Fire, by contrast, is placed beside the sphere because its lightness and brightness suit that position. If another element were placed there, it would be heated by the sphere’s continual motion until it became fire; then the heat of fire would be added to it, burning the other elements until everything became fire and all life was destroyed.

From the beginning, God’s care called for rational and non-rational souls to exist. They needed animal and plant bodies, most of whose material is dry. Dryness helps preserve forms and shapes. So the earth had to be cold and dry, with parts that hold together, so animals and plants—whose bodies contain much of this element—could live beside it. For the same wise reason, water does not completely surround the earth: most animals and plants need to breathe air and draw it in. Air is placed beside fire because they share heat and lightness; water lies between air and earth because it shares lightness with air and coldness with earth, preserving the balance among them.

passage-en-00407

Consider also this: if the layers of elements and spheres above the earth were opaque and colored, rather than clear, the light of the stars would stop at their surfaces or be reflected upwards, away from the world of change and decay. Those living in the depths of matter would be left in a terrible darkness. So the stars were made bright, and the spheres and the other elements clear. If all the elements could receive light, their heat would grow so intense that everything in this world would burn.

XII. An example of His care in creating compound beings
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00409

Can you not see, seeker of knowledge, how God gave the elements heat that dissolves, refines, and sets things in motion; cold that steadies and holds things together; moisture that can receive shapes and be divided; and dryness that preserves the shapes and order it receives? He formed living things from mixtures of the elements, gave each kind of perfection a fitting balance of qualities, and granted every prepared thing the perfection it was ready to receive. He did not stop there. He also gave each thing guidance toward further perfections and ends, so that it could rise along the upward path to higher levels. This is what our Lord means when He says: “Our Lord is the One who gave everything its form, then guided it.”
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00410

Consider the bodies of plants and animals. They are always breaking down, so God gave them a power to take in food, digest it, and change it into a substance like their own. Since plants and animals cannot reach their full size in an instant, He also placed in them a power of growth. It increases the size of the nourished body in each direction according to the proportions suited to it.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00411

Rejoice, seeker of knowledge, and remember your Lord’s mercy. Praise Him for how the generosity of the true Giver completes what would otherwise be missing from lasting existence. Some things last as individuals, while others last only as kinds. He makes up for the short life of each individual by preserving its kind through a succession of individuals. In this way, the natural world is ordered through both kinds of endurance. Consider plants and animals, which generally continue only by reproducing. God placed a power of generation in their reproductive organs. It takes what is left over from the material that formed one individual and uses it to begin another, so that the kind continues even though the individual must perish.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00412

Consider how God created a desire for food and the pleasure of sex in beings whose actions are voluntary rather than purely natural or forced. Such a being is like a worker who will not do the work without being paid. The desires that move an animal’s soul to perform the actions needed to preserve its own life and its kind are like wages for a worker or payment to servants and helpers. They prevent the animal from neglecting the purpose of these actions.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00413

Consider, too, how the power that takes in food has four powers to help it: one draws food in; another breaks it down and prepares it for the body to use; a third holds it in place while it is being changed; and a fourth removes what cannot be made like the body. Animals are nobler than plants, so they have further powers: the ability to perceive and the ability to move. The animal soul senses and chooses how to move its body.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00414

The human body has a finer balance of qualities. God gave it a spiritual reality: when it obeys its Lord and is completed through knowledge and action, it rises into the world of spirits, draws near to its source by cutting its ties to the bodily world, and becomes like the highest company of angels and the people of the world of power. If you think carefully about how the soul governs the body, how they become attached to one another, how the soul longs to act through the body, and how painful their separation is—even though the body is heavy and dense while the soul is subtle and light—you will be astonished. How can light and darkness, what is free from matter and what is material, be joined? How can the higher realm, which God honors by saying, “We raised him to a high place,” and, “The record of the righteous is in the highest place,” be joined to the lower realm, which He describes by saying, “The record of the wicked is in a prison”? The difference between them is clear to anyone who reflects.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00415

Most people—and perhaps everyone except a very few—are unaware of, or even deny, this connection and union between soul and body. Even many who claim to be learned deny that the soul exists apart from the body. Most who do believe that it does imagine that a person’s humanity comes from another species-form impressed on the body, and that the two together make a human being. They take the “I”—the rational soul—to be something else, merely attached to the body because it is the tool of the soul’s bodily actions. In our view, they have not understood the soul or its stages of descent and ascent. As we explained earlier, the soul is the same being that takes nourishment, grows, moves, rests, eats, drinks, touches, smells, and tastes.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00416

See the Maker’s wisdom: He makes what is subtle dense—or rather, through His wise care, makes what is dense subtle. From the finest part of the elements He formed the dense body from which the human being is made, beginning with the substance of semen. From its finest part and cream He formed the cone-shaped heart, and from the finest part of the blood He formed the pure blood.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00417

From the purest part of that blood comes the vital spirit, a fine vapour that flows from the body’s chief organ. In its clarity and balance, it is like a distant sphere, far removed from conflict. It is balanced between opposites while gathering qualities from both ends, like the seven firm heavens. Its brightness is like the stars that shine before our eyes. Because it is clear and smooth, it becomes a mirror in which the forms of real things shine and sensory images appear. These images stand between the two worlds. In a way, this substance is the soul’s home and is united with it when its own life-bearing substance rises from the power of the soul to the level of intellect. The soul, in turn, is the material for intellect and is united with it when its own being rises from potentiality to actuality. The vital spirit is a mirror in which the soul appears, and the soul is a mirror in which intellect appears.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00418

The human being passes through these stages in its own being, changing little by little from semen to intellect. It brings together the two worlds, the visible and the spiritual. In it there is something like a sphere, a mirror for perceiving individual things, both present and absent; and something like an angel, a mirror for perceiving universal truths that do not change. Consider this power and wisdom, then this subtlety and mercy. The wonders of God’s presence will leave you amazed. If you want a fuller explanation, listen.

XIII. Signs of God’s wisdom and care in creating the human being
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00420

Human beings begin as the lowliest things, made from the least complete material and the weakest bodies. They begin as matter that has the capacity to become something but is not yet any definite thing, then come to be from dark dust and clinging clay, and then from semen. The divine Book points to the first stage when it says: “Has there not been a time when the human being was nothing worth mentioning?” It points to the next stages when it says: “We created the human being from a mixed drop to test him,” and, “He is the One who created you from dust, then from a drop.”
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00421

After these stages, the human being develops the powers and organs of plant life. Then comes animal life, as God says: “We made him hearing and seeing.” The human being gradually acquires all the powers of animal life, beginning with touch and ending with the power that makes judgments about particular things. Then another creation begins, as God says: “Then We brought him into being in another form. Blessed is God, the best of creators.”
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00422

Look, you who study the signs within and around you, at the semen: a dirty, watery fluid whose balance would break down if it were left for even an hour. See how the Lord of lords brings it forth from between the backbone and the ribs, protects it from dispersing, and places it in a secure resting place. He changes it from a white fluid into a red clot, then into a lump of flesh. He divides its similar parts into bones, nerves, veins, tendons, flesh, and other simple organs. Then He joins those simple organs into more complex ones—the head, hands, feet, and other parts—and shapes each for the work it is meant to do, as the principles of anatomy and other sciences make clear. He creates all this in the womb, within three layers of darkness. If the veil were lifted and your sight could reach inside, you would see lines and shapes gradually appear, though you would see no tool at work. Glory be to the One who shapes, without any tool or finger visible in His shaping.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00423

When the growing body reaches the stage where it draws in food and grows, God gives it plant life, with many powers to serve it. Angels are appointed to these powers, and through them the body is nourished and grows. See how God appoints angels to keep your affairs in order—even your nourishment. Those who see with the inner sight of their hearts say that each part of the body is nourished only with the help of at least seven angels, perhaps ten, a hundred, a thousand, or more. Nourishment means that a part of food takes the place of a part of the body that has worn away. To do so, the food changes through several stages, until at last it becomes blood, then flesh and bone.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00424

Food is a body. It does not move or change by itself through all these stages. Wheat does not become flour, then sifted flour, then dough, then a round loaf baked in an oven without the work of makers. In the hidden world, when a work serves a wise purpose, its makers are angels, just as human beings are the makers of visible things. God has given you His visible and hidden blessings, though people often overlook the hidden ones.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00425

A person of insight knows that seven angels are needed. The first draws food to the organs. The second holds it beside the organ. The third strips away its former shape and changes it into blood. The fourth gives it the form of flesh, bone, and other tissues. The fifth removes what is left over. The sixth joins new flesh to flesh and bone to bone, so nothing remains detached. The seventh oversees the amounts and proportions as the parts are joined.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00426

You might ask: why not assign all these tasks to one angel? Why are seven needed? Wheat also needs one person to grind it, another to sift it, a third to add water, a fourth to knead it, a fifth to divide it into round pieces, a sixth to roll them into flat loaves, and a seventh to place them against the oven. Why do the angels’ hidden tasks not work like the visible tasks done by people?
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00427

The answer is that angels are made differently from human beings. Their being is simple and has no mixture of parts, and their actions do not conflict with one another. Their qualities and beings do not compete, and each angel has only one task. God points to this when He says: “There is not one of us who does not have a known place.” So they do not quarrel or struggle, and their actions and qualities do not conflict. Their order is like the order of our senses: sight does not compete with hearing, whose task is to perceive sounds; smell does not compete with sight or hearing in perceiving scents; taste and the other senses do not interfere with one another either.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00428

The senses are unlike the body’s limbs. The toes can grasp weakly; some people write with their toes, and others walk on their hands. You might strike someone with your head, making it compete with the hand, which is the usual tool for striking. Nor are angels like a person who grinds, kneads, and bakes the bread alone. Such a person’s work is disordered and falls short of what is right because human qualities and motives differ. A human being does not have one single way of acting: sometimes people disobey God, and sometimes they obey Him. Angels cannot do this. They are made to obey, with no possibility of sin: “They do not disobey God in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded.” They praise Him night and day without tiring. The angel who bows is always bowing; the one who prostrates is always prostrating; the one who stands is always standing.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00429

Here is a subtle point. Someone might say: if every angel is assigned one task and cannot move on to another, then it is limited and unable to do many good things. The answer is that every angel’s being is connected to the being of the angel above it, which sustains it and gives it life—not by joining together like bodily parts, but in another way. Each angel is one in being and one in its task, yet many different actions can issue from it. They follow one another in an ordered sequence that never changes. You have learned that order gathers many things into one. So the angels’ actions rise toward a single action from which their many effects branch out. In the same way, their many beings return to one being with which they are united. Each angel lives and knows through the life and knowledge of the angel below its command and care. This is unlike our body parts, which are unaware of themselves and of what they do.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00430

The angels stand in relation to those under their command as our powers of perception stand in relation to the rational spirit within us. As we have explained, each sense and each image present to the soul is alive through the soul’s life. Yet each sense has its own task, distinct from the others, with no mixing or confusion. The senses come from the higher, active side of the soul, not from the receptive side, like the limbs and similar parts.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00431

Let us return to our subject. Plant life, together with the helpers God created for nourishment and reproduction, makes a human being more complete than stones, crystals, iron, copper, gold, silver, and other minerals. But plant life is still incomplete. Food may not reach a plant or touch its roots, and the plant may dry out because it cannot seek food or move from one place to another. Seeking requires two things—knowledge and power—and plants lack them. If human existence stopped at this level, it would be incomplete and helpless in what it could do. See how God raised the human being beyond this stage by giving it another form of life, setting it apart from plants and lifting it above lifeless things. In one more step, He brought it nearer to the Lord of lords and the source of light, away from the depths of darkness. He gave it the tools of sensation and voluntary movement, so it could seek food. The Book points to this: “We made him hearing and seeing,” and, “We showed him the way, whether he is grateful or ungrateful.”
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00432

Now consider God’s wise arrangement of the five senses. Touch comes first. It is the least complete sense, since it detects only what touches or is joined to the animal, not what is far away. Sensing distant things requires a stronger, more complete sense. Touch is found in all animals. Some lowly animals, close to plant life, such as worms in the soil, have only touch and cannot seek food. If you had been given no sense beyond touch, you would be incomplete like a worm. You therefore needed another sense to detect what is far away, and God gave you smell. But smell does not tell you which direction a scent comes from, so you might wander around for a long time before finding its source.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00433

Then God gave you sight. But sight cannot detect what is hidden behind a wall or another barrier, and it detects only what is present before you. You cannot learn about what is absent unless someone tells you about it. You receive that report through speech and signs heard by the sense of hearing. So your need for hearing became great. See how God blessed you and set you apart from other animals by giving you the ability to understand speech. Yet all this would not help you if you had no sense of taste. When food reaches you, you would not know whether it suited you or harmed you. You might eat it and die, like a tree that draws in water that dries it out because it has no taste to warn it.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00434

Even all this would not complete human life without an inner power that receives the forms of the five senses, preserves them, and recalls them. Otherwise, you would have to learn every sensible thing again whenever you encountered it, because its image would not be stored within you. So God gave you other inward senses to preserve what you perceive, bring it back to mind when you wish, and work with it. Animals share these powers with you. If you had no more than these, you would still be incomplete, because you could not understand the outcomes and rational purposes of things. God distinguished and honored you above many of His creatures by giving you another power: reason. It can recognise what is harmful and what is useful in the long term, and grasp true goods and future harms.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00435

This is one example of God’s gifts to you in the realm of perception. As for the other group of powers—the powers that move you, which are also among God’s forces—and how they are arranged within you, consider this. If you could perceive the things needed to develop and preserve your life in this world, including food, whether near or far, but had no natural inclination, appetite, or longing to move you towards them, and no bodily ability to act, then your perceptions would be useless.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00436

You therefore need an inclination toward what suits you, called appetite, and an aversion to what conflicts with you, called dislike. God placed in you an appetite for food to preserve your individual life and a desire for sex to preserve the human kind. These desires press you to eat and act like a claimant demanding payment.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00437

If appetite did not subside once you had enough of what you wanted, you would overeat and destroy yourself. So God gave you dislike when you are full, and when you have enough in similar ways, so that you stop eating and doing other things. A plant, by contrast, keeps drawing in water as it flows to its roots until it is ruined. It needs a human being to give it only as much food as it requires.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00438

You have also learned that you have a natural power, shared with plants, that spreads through the whole body and begins in the liver; another power, shared with animals, that spreads through the organs and begins in the heart; another, more specialised power of the soul, shared with some animals and beginning in the brain; and a still higher power, which animals do not share—only angels do. Each of these gives you a way to approach or withdraw from what benefits or harms you. The two responses belonging to the first power are called attraction and repulsion; those belonging to the second are inclination and aversion; those belonging to the third are desire and anger; and those belonging to the fourth are will and avoidance.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00439

God made the last pair answer to reason, which recognises the consequences of actions. He made desire and anger answer to sensory perception. This allows you to make use of reason. Simply knowing that something will harm you or benefit you is not enough to make you avoid or seek it. You also need a will that follows what you know, or an aversion that turns you away from it. Through this will, God set you apart from animals, honoring human beings, just as He set you apart from them through your ability to understand consequences.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00440
XIV. God’s care in creating the earth and what it contains for human benefit
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00441

God says: “He created for you everything on earth.” Now that you have seen God’s care in creating you and your body, look at the signs of His mercy in what lies outside you. The nearest thing outside you is the ground on which you rest. Consider the earth, the home of your body and the mother of the body that was first within her, then born from her, and will return to her again. God says: “From it We created you, to it We will return you, and from it We will bring you out once more.” Then consider its benefits.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00442

The earth is like a bed and resting place on which you can sleep, and a surface on which you can walk, as God says: “He made the earth a bed,” and, “God made the earth spread out for you, so that you may travel along its wide paths.” A bed does not have to be flat. A very large sphere can also provide a good surface for rest and walking. But for that to be possible, the earth must remain in its natural place, at the center of the heavenly spheres. God points to this when He says: “God is the One who made the earth a place of rest.” Heavy things naturally move downwards, while light things move upwards. “Up” on every side is toward the sky, and “down” is toward the center.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00443

Another of God’s gifts is that He did not make the earth as hard as iron or stone, so that food could grow from it, wells could be dug, and rivers could flow. Nor did He make it as soft and yielding as water, so that we could sleep and walk on it, farm it, and build with it. He did not make it so fine and transparent that light would pass through it and it could not be walked on. He also let part of it rise above the water, even though its natural tendency is to sink into it, so that we and the land animals could live there. One reason for the exposed land is that God made the earth and water, through the blowing of winds, the flow of rivers, and the movement of seas, not perfectly round. When water settles into the lower parts, some land remains uncovered, and the earth and its surrounding water together form a sphere.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00444

We know that the earth is round because stars rise and set earlier for people in the east than for people in the west. From north to south, the visible pole rises higher for those traveling north, and the reverse happens for those traveling south. Travelers moving along paths between these directions see both effects. There are other signs of the earth’s roundness too, including the way eclipses begin and end at different times in different places. A particular eclipse begins at the start of night in one place, an hour later in another, two hours later in another, and after a quarter, a third, or half the night elsewhere. These differences follow a measured pattern based on how far apart the places are, both east to west and north to south. The same is true for people traveling over land and by sea.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00445

The earth also brings forth minerals, plants, and animals. It draws down water from the sky, as God says: “We sent water down from the sky in due measure and let it settle in the earth.” It has springs and great rivers, as He says: “We spread out the earth.” It opens up to plants and other growth: “By the earth that splits open.” Its life and death remind people of their own death and resurrection. God says: “A sign for them is the dead earth; We bring it to life,” and, “We bring the earth to life after its death. That is how the dead will be raised.” He also says: “Look at the signs of God’s mercy: how He brings the earth to life after its death. He will surely bring the dead to life; He has power over all things.” And: “Among His signs is that you see the earth lying still; then, when We send water down on it, it stirs and swells. The One who brought it to life will surely bring the dead to life. He has power over all things.”
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00446

The earth also produces many kinds of animals and spreads every sort of living creature across it. Some are food; others are livestock, whose wool and hides keep you warm and whose other benefits serve you. God says: “He created livestock for you. In them you have warmth and many benefits, and from them you eat.” Some animals are for riding and adornment: “Horses, mules, and donkeys, for you to ride and as an adornment.” Some carry heavy loads to places you could reach only with great effort: “They carry your loads to a land you could not reach without great hardship. Your Lord is kind and merciful.” Some bring comfort and beauty, when they come home in the evening and go out to pasture in the morning. Some are created as mates: “God made spouses for you from among yourselves.” Others provide clothing, shelter, and household goods: “He made homes for you from the hides of livestock, easy to carry on the day you travel and the day you settle; and from their wool, fur, and hair, furnishings and useful things for a time.”
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00447

The earth also grows plants of many kinds: “We made every lovely kind of plant grow in it.” Their different colors are a sign and a mercy; their different scents offer guidance and care. Some plants feed people and others feed animals: “Eat and graze your livestock.” They are a provision for you and your animals. From plants come food and seasonings, medicines, and fruits: “He grows grain, olives, date palms, grapevines, and every kind of fruit.” Plants also provide clothing: cotton and flax, and, from animals that live on plants, hair, wool, silk, and leather.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00448

The earth yields stones of many colors and degrees of clarity. God says: “Among the mountains are white and red paths, of different colors, and others intensely black.” Some stones are used for adornment; others for buildings. Compare the common stone that gives us fire with the rare red ruby. The common stone is used far more, while the rare gem is used little. The earth also holds precious metals such as gold and silver. Human beings have developed delicate crafts and great industries, brought fish up from the bottom of the sea, and drawn birds down from the heights of the air. Yet they cannot make gold and silver. The reason is that their chief use is as money, and that use depends on their being rare and hard to obtain. If people could make them freely, their purpose would be lost. That is why God has closed the door to making them. As the saying goes, whoever seeks wealth through alchemy ends up poor.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00449

The earth is also generous by nature: it takes one seed and returns seven hundred, as the Qur'an says. People have disagreed, based on reports, about whether heaven or earth is nobler. Some say heaven is nobler because it is the place where angels worship and no part of it has disobeyed God; its inhabitants are protected from error and disobedience. When our father Adam sinned, he was sent down from the garden. God says: “He does not let those who disobey Me remain in My presence.” He calls heaven a protected roof and praises its constellations in many verses. Others say the earth is nobler because God has called certain places blessed: “The first House established for people was the one at Bakkah, blessed,” and, “Glory be to the One who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed.” He also says: “The east and west of the earth, which We blessed,” meaning the land of Syria. He describes the whole earth as blessed: “He placed blessings in it and measured its provisions.” Someone might ask: what blessing is there in empty, deadly deserts? We reply that they are homes to creatures known only to God. This is why He says: “On earth are signs for those who are certain.”
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00450

The truth is that heaven is adorned with stars, the stars with spiritual angels, and the earth with forms and animal souls. The earth’s adornment includes human spirits, which make use of its resources, and their adornment is their divine knowledge, which they share with the angels brought near to God. Heaven’s outward aspect is nobler than earth’s, but inwardly the two are the other way around, because the end is nobler than what leads to it. The earth is also like a gift and a pearl containing Adam and his children. God taught Adam what they would need and said, in effect: “I will not leave you in need of anything beyond this earth, which is like a mother to you.” He says: “We poured down water in abundance, then split the earth open,” and: “He sent water down from the sky and brought forth fruits as provision for you. My servant, the things you value most are gold and silver. If I had made the earth out of them, could it have provided these benefits? I made these things available for you in this world, though this world is a prison for you. What, then, will it be like in the garden?”
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00451
XV. The wonders of God’s work in the celestial bodies and the lights of the stars
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00452

Now that you have seen an example of the earth’s benefits, raise your head to the sky. Look and reflect on how the heavens were made, on their stars, and on their ordered movements, their rising and setting, and their different points of sunrise and sunset. The sun, moon, Jupiter, and Saturn move constantly, seeking God and longing to meet Him without weariness, delay, or change in their courses. They travel through measured stations, according to a precise reckoning and a written record, until their appointed time. God says: “We have set the moon through stages.” It neither goes beyond them nor falls short, until God folds them up like a scroll.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00453

Consider the number of stars, how many bright ones there are, and how their colors differ. Their colors are not like the changing, decaying colors we see on earth. Their shapes are of a higher kind, as are their tastes, scents, and sounds. They descend from the heavens to the earth, so there they are more subtle, pure, and simple. Every form on earth has a higher likeness in heaven. God has many purposes for each star: in its creation, form, size, shape, position, relation to other stars, and distance from the center of the sky. Compare the wisdom shown in these arrangements with the care given to the organs of your small body. The heavens are incomparably greater than a human being. God says: “Are you harder to create, or the heaven? He built it.” Even within the earthly world, compare the differences in size and subtlety between things with the differences in their wonderful arrangement, fine order, and remarkable natural forms.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00454

Have you not considered the kingdom of the heavens and the stars within them, how their being is sustained, their light shines, and they obey their Maker through their movements, out of love and longing for Him? Do you not hear how God speaks of their greatness and honors the stars in His Book? Many chapters describe the greatness and glory of heaven, and God swears by it: “By the sun and its brightness,” “By the moon as it follows it,” “By the star when it falls,” and, “I swear by the positions of the stars—if you only knew, that is a tremendous oath.”
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00455

God praises those who reflect on the heavens and earth: “They reflect on the creation of the heavens and earth.” He condemns those who turn away from them: “They turn away from its signs.” He made the heavens a protected roof, raised high above us, and kept devils from entering because heaven is a place of worship and purity, inhabited by angels who praise and glorify God. Defiled souls stained by disbelief and idolatry cannot enter its sacred place, just as people stained by idolatry are not allowed to enter the Sacred Mosque on earth. God says: “The idolaters are impure, so they must not approach the Sacred Mosque.”
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00456

Look into heaven’s spiritual realm and you will see wonders of might and power. Let your thought travel far through the visible heavens. Perhaps its gates will open to you and you will enter the garden, leaving this dark pit for the world of light. Let your heart travel through its regions until you stand before the Throne of the All-Merciful. Then we may hope that you will reach the highest rank—but only after passing beyond the levels of this lower world. The signs of heaven’s nobility are too many to count, as are its benefits for human beings.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00457

Among them is the wise purpose and sound end in its creation. God says: “Our Lord, You did not create this without purpose,” and, “We did not create the heaven, the earth, and all that lies between them in vain. That is what those who disbelieve suppose.” He adorned it with lamps: “We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps.” He placed the moon among them as a light and the sun as a lamp. He called heaven a protected roof, seven layers, and seven strong heavens. He made it a path by which good actions rise and good words ascend—the perfected souls, complete in knowledge and action. God says: “A good word is like a good tree, whose roots are firm and whose branches reach the sky,” and, “Good words rise to Him, and He raises up righteous deeds.”
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00458

Heaven is also the direction toward which prayers rise and the source of light and radiance. God brought lights and colors down from it into the earthly world. Its colors, shapes, sounds, melodies, and other qualities are the finest, and its places are the highest because they are far from opposition and decay. They benefit God’s servants. Its stars are signs that guide travelers across the darkness of land and sea. The sun rises at a time that lets people go about their needs in every region, and sets at a time that brings calm and quiet, so that they may rest, digest food, and let it reach their organs, or escape their enemies. God says: “We made the night a covering,” “We made the day for work,” and, “He made the night a time of rest.”
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00459

If the sun never rose, the waters would freeze, cold and density would take over, and the body’s natural warmth would weaken and die. If it never set, the earth would grow so hot that every animal on it would burn. The sun is like a lamp brought into a house for as long as its inhabitants need it, then taken away so they can settle down and rest. Light and darkness, though opposite, work together for the well-being of those who live on earth.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00460

It is as though God were saying: if the sun stayed on one side of the sky, north or south, a rich person might build a house on a hill above a poor person’s home and block the light. But I move the heavens and guide the sun so that the poor receive their share of daylight just as the rich do.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00461

As we have seen, the sun’s height and descent bring about the four seasons. In winter, heat retreats into trees and plants, where food and fruit take shape, and animals grow stronger because their natural warmth gathers inside them. In spring, nature stirs, the substances formed in winter come forth, trees grow bright with leaves and flowers, and animals are driven to reproduce. In summer, the air grows hot, fruits ripen, excess moisture leaves the body, and the earth dries, ready for buildings and farming. In autumn, cold and dryness set in, fruits mature, and bodies gradually prepare for winter.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00462

The moon follows the sun and acts as its deputy. It helps us count years, measure time, and set the religious times for prayer, fasting, and pilgrimage. It also helps plants grow and thrive. Its rising and setting, and its changing shapes from crescent to full moon, serve many purposes known only to God.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00463

Al-Jāḥiẓ said: “If you reflect on the world we live in, you will find that it is like a house equipped with everything needed. The sky is raised like a roof, the earth spread out like a carpet, the stars set in place like lamps, and the human being is like the owner who manages the house. All kinds of plants are prepared for human use, and all kinds of animals are put to work for human benefit.” I would add that if you look at the heavenly world, with its vastness and countless stars, you will find an inhabited house, one of those houses that God has permitted to be raised, where His name is remembered. It contains many kinds of worshippers: some remain prostrate and never bow; others remain bowed and never stand upright. They praise God without weariness. Their eyes do not sleep, their bodies do not tire, and forgetfulness does not overcome them.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00464

A house need not be made of physical things in order to be a home. God says: “The home of the next life is truly life.” Nor must a place of worship be built from clay, stone, and wood. God says: “Only those who believe in God and the Last Day, and keep up prayer, maintain God’s mosques.” A place of worship need not even be a physical building. Wherever worship, remembrance, praise, and sanctification take place, there is a house of worship.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00465

Consider how the Maker, exalted be His name, built the heavens as a place of worship for angels who praise, glorify, and remember God. He holds them up without pillars that you can see, and without a rope or support hanging them in place. It is astonishing that someone can fail to look at or reflect on a house that God built by His power, made and adorned by Himself, and filled with all kinds of decoration and images. Forgetting himself and failing to be present in heart, he forgets his Lord and thinks only of food, sex, status, and reputation. It is astonishing that he can enter a rich person’s house, see its painted and gilded walls, and never stop marvelling at it or praising the one who built and decorated it—yet remain unaware of God’s great house and of the angels who live in His heavens.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00466

He gives heaven no thought. He knows no more about it than an animal knows about the roof above it, or an ant knows about the ceiling of its nest. He knows no more about the angels of heaven or their wondrous forms than an ant knows about the minds of those in its home or the patterns on its walls. How deep is this carelessness, this sleep that overwhelms most people, this intoxication, this great ignorance, this misery that surrounds them! Come, seeker of knowledge, let us praise and sanctify our Lord. Come, seeker of truth, let us proclaim His oneness and greatness. Let us call upon the One who sustains the world, orders the seen and unseen realms, joins the human world to the divine, and possesses all majesty and power—with grieving hearts, present minds, remembering tongues, chests opened by the light of knowledge, and flowing tears. Hurry, seeker of knowledge, with an eager spirit and a pure soul, in love with its Lord and returning to Him. Let us call to Him quietly and plead with Him in the darkness of night. Let us pray as lovers who sigh, as the humble who bow, and as those who long for Him and know their need. Glory be to You; there is no god but You. Save us from the fire of separation and the pain of being cut off. You bring the dead to life and raise spirits from their worn-out graves. You give good things and send down blessings. Pour the gleams of Your blessing upon our souls and the bright rays of Your goodness upon our spirits. You are the One whose presence makes all things bow; You sprinkle Your light upon dark beings and shadowed bodies in the deepest night, giving them light and form, stirring in them longing for Your beauty and leading them to seek Your presence. You cast the spark of Your longing upon the heavens, setting them in motion and making them circle. You set all who are in them to move in love, leading them to circle the Ancient House once every seven thousand years. Free us by Your light from the darkness of the grave.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00467

Do not torment our souls with their ties to the bodies of this deceptive world, the source of delusion. Keep our feet firm on the bright and straight path, the true and upright way. You are generous and kind, the giver of goodness and mercy.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00468

This is one example of God’s subtle care and kindness in the visible world. No one can hope to know every detail of the mercy and care hidden in His unseen realm, or to explore every wonder of His work and wisdom in the beings around us, even over a long lifetime. The knowledge of the learned is slight compared with what the prophets and saints know; their knowledge is slight beside that of the angels brought near to God, and of the highest people among humankind when they stand before Him. When all the knowledge of angels, spirits, and human beings is compared with God’s knowledge, it hardly deserves to be called knowledge. It is closer to bewilderment, confusion, helplessness, and limitation than to understanding and wisdom. True wisdom is knowing things as they really are. As we have already explained, to know a thing fully is to have its very being. Only its Maker and source can encompass it. No one is truly wise except God alone. Wisdom and knowledge are applied to others only by comparison and metaphor. That is why everyone is addressed by God’s words: “You have been given only a little knowledge.”
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00469
XVI. All beings love God, long to meet Him, and seek His home of honor
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00470

Know that God has given every being—intellectual, spiritual, sensory, and natural—its own perfection. He has placed in each one love and longing for that perfection, and a movement toward completing it. Love without longing belongs to intellects that exist apart from matter and are fully actual in every way. Other beings lack some perfection and have the potential and readiness to gain it. They therefore have love and longing, either by choice or by nature, in different degrees. A movement then follows, matching that inclination. It may be a movement of the soul or of the body. Bodily movement may be a change in quality, as in natural compounds; a change in size, especially in animals and plants; a change in position, as in the heavenly bodies; or a change of place, as in the elements.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00471

Here is the proof. You have learned that all existence is good, valuable, and pleasant, while its opposite, non-existence, is evil, repellent, and something we flee from. Existence is one simple reality in itself. It differs only through limits and levels, which give rise to the different kinds and classes of possible things. Existence varies only in being more or less complete, strong, or weak. Its highest perfection is the Necessary Being, the Real, whose perfection has no limit. Every caused being receives a share of that perfection from Him, and has a limit because it is caused. Existence itself, simply as existence, does not require lack, limitation, or change. If it did, the Necessary Being could not have limitless power and perfection. Lack and limitation therefore belong to caused beings. An effect cannot equal its cause in rank; if it did, neither would be the cause rather than the other.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00472

The one who is not caused by anything else—God, the Necessary Being—has no lack. He is pure existence and pure good, and so the greatest source of joy and love. He loves Himself and all the good things that belong to Him. The more a being depends on causes and intermediaries between itself and the pure Real, the less complete it is. The closer it is to God, the more complete it is. So every being has some share of divine love, divine care, and God’s love for it. If it were without this for even a moment, it would vanish and perish. Every being loves existence, seeks to complete its existence, and turns away from non-existence and lack.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00473

Whatever is sought can be preserved and continued only through what completes it. An effect lasts only through its cause, because the cause completes it. Heat lasts only through stronger heat, and light becomes complete only through stronger light. Uncertain, incomplete knowledge becomes complete when a proof grounded in reason turns it into lasting certainty. In the same way, an incomplete being can become complete only through something stronger than itself: its cause. The cause sustains it and makes it what it is. Matter is completed only through form; form, only through what gives it form; sensation, only through the soul; the soul, only through intellect; and intellect lasts only through the Necessary Being. Every incomplete thing therefore turns away from its lack and reaches toward its perfection. Once it gains that perfection, it holds on to it. Every being must love its perfection and long for it when it lacks it. A being therefore always loves its perfection, whether it has it or is without it.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00474

Longing and inclination arise only when a being lacks its perfection. Love, then, runs through all beings, while longing belongs only to those that can lack something. We have also explained more than once that life runs through all beings because existence runs through them. Existence is one reality, and it is the same as knowledge, power, and life. Just as nothing can exist without existence itself, nothing can exist without some kind of knowledge and action. Whatever knows and acts in any way is alive. So, in the view of those who know these things directly, everything is alive. Most people, however, use the word “animal” only for a being with outward senses and the ability to choose where it moves.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00475

If every simple or compound being has some life and awareness, it must also have love and longing. Look at beings and their levels of existence. Each is either complete in every way or lacking in some way. A being complete in every way is complete either through itself or through something beyond itself. In the first case, the being and its perfection are one and the same, both in reality and in how we think of them. The first is the Necessary Being; the second is the intellectual beings. Neither kind is without love, and for both, love is their very being. The Necessary Being loves only Himself: He is beloved by Himself and by everything other than Himself. Intellectual beings love Him, not themselves except insofar as they are His effects. Their love for themselves is lost in their love for the First. Their light of existence is likewise swallowed up in the light of God’s oneness. In truth, there is one connected love with different levels, some surrounding others. God encompasses all that lies beyond them.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00476

The second group—beings that are not complete in every way—either have what they need to rise from lack to perfection within themselves and their own cause, or they do not. The first are the souls of the heavenly spheres. They have perfection in one respect and lack it in another, so they love and long without end. They feel the pleasure of connection and the pain of separation. Their pleasure does not belong only to one time and their pain only to another. Instead, their pain is mixed with pleasure, and because it comes from the experience of love, it is a pleasurable pain. To describe these souls’ longing for intellectual perfection and spiritual beloveds, philosophers used a distant comparison: the state of someone who has an itch or is being tickled.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00477

The second group is either incomplete in every way or incomplete in one respect but not another. A being in the latter class may have no perfection beyond the basic nature of its body. These are the lowest bodily kinds, such as the four elements, whose own natures are limited and opposed to one another. Or it may have some added perfection beyond its bodily nature.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00478

The first kind, because its own substance is incomplete, can be combined with other kinds. When combined, the elements’ opposition is reduced, and they receive another kind of life. This life preserves their structure for a time, keeping one opposite from destroying the others. If the form that preserves them from destruction by opposites is their only perfection, the result is an inanimate thing. If it also seeks individual growth and the continuation of its kind through reproduction, it is a plant. If it goes further and receives forms that are not material in themselves, while its senses and tools draw those forms from material things, it is an animal. Animals gain strength through sensation and imagination, just as plants gain strength through nourishment and growth.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00479

Each of these incomplete beings clearly seeks the perfection that completes its existence. The form that holds a compound body together becomes more complete when it gains the power to increase the individual’s size. It draws in food, changes it into a substance like its own, and joins it to the body in the right proportions. It also increases the number of individuals in its kind through reproduction.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00480

Once it reaches this perfection and, with it, comes a little closer to the First, who is perfect in every way, it seeks a fuller perfection, one closer to true completeness. It becomes able to sense, then to imagine, then to remember. It becomes able to understand basic truths as a settled ability, then to grasp further truths through thought. It then becomes an intellect that is simple and fully active in understanding. At last, it returns to God, content and accepted by Him. These stages come through a series of longings and experiences: each love is a cause that leads toward the next beloved, which becomes the end of that earlier love. This continues until the being reaches the Beloved of all beloveds, the end of every pleasure and desire, and the final goal of all movement.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00481

The first kind in the second group, which is incomplete in every way, is bodily matter. In itself, it is the potential for everything, and has no existence apart from the forms that enter it. Its very nature is need and dependence—in fact, a longing for every form of perfection that has become actual. The Shaykh, Ibn Sina, strongly denied in the natural-science section of The Healing that matter longs for forms, as earlier thinkers had said. Yet in his treatise on love and its spread through all beings, he admitted that it does. He explained this love by saying that matter is never without a form, but is always clothed in one. He explained the love of the simple elements and compounds of minerals by their natural movement to their proper places, and the love in plants by their powers of nourishment, growth, and reproduction. He did not claim that these beings have awareness or life.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00482

To say that something loves without being alive or aware is only to give it a name. In the First Journey, when discussing cause and effect, we proved that matter loves form. We also showed that life and awareness are present throughout all beings. This is the key to the present discussion. Ibn Sina did not establish it, nor did anyone after him up to our own time, except the mystics who know by direct insight. Through their own experience and by following the light of the Book and the Prophet’s teachings, they saw that all things are alive, speak, remember God, praise Him, and bow before Him. The Qur'an says: “There is nothing that does not praise Him, though you do not understand their praise.” It also says: “To God bows everything in the heavens and the earth.” By God’s grace, we have come to know this through both proof and faith. This insight has been given to us through God’s favor and kind guidance.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00483

What the Shaykh, one of the greatest philosophers of this Islamic age, managed to say about love in simple beings that he thought were lifeless is found in his treatise. He says that there are three such simple beings. The first is prime matter; the second is form, which cannot stand on its own; the third is an accident. Form differs from matter because it makes a substance what it is. For this reason, the early thinkers who believed in God kept form among the kinds of substance: it is part of substances that exist on their own. They did not deny that form is a kind of substance just because it cannot exist by itself. Prime matter is in the same position, yet it is not strange to count it among substances because it is part of substances that exist on their own.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00484

Form also has a greater claim to being called a substance than matter does, because form makes a substance into an actual substance. Wherever form exists, an actual substance must exist too. So form has been called a substance in the active sense. Matter, on the other hand, is only able to receive substance. It is called a substance in the potential sense: the presence of matter does not mean an actual substance must be present. This explains what form really is. It should not be treated as an accident.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00485

Once this is clear, we can say that each simple being thought to be lifeless is joined to a natural love that never leaves it and is a cause of its existence. As for matter, it is always reaching toward form. It lacks form in itself, but is made into different kinds of things through form. When it is stripped of one form, it quickly receives another because it fears remaining in complete non-existence. Matter turns away from non-existence. When it has a form, only a relative absence remains in it; without form, it would be covered by complete non-existence. There is no need here to explain the cause of this in detail. Matter is like an unattractive woman afraid to reveal her ugliness: whenever she lifts her veil, she covers her face with makeup. This establishes a natural love in matter.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00486

Natural love in form is clear for two reasons. First, form makes every effort to remain in the matter that supports it and resists being stripped away from it. Second, when it has reached its natural place, it tries to remain there; when it is moved away, it moves with longing back toward that place. This applies to the forms of the five simple bodies and to compounds made from the four elements.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00487

The only other forms are accidents. Their love is shown by their effort to remain in their subject, even as they follow one another when that subject changes. So none of these simple beings is without a natural love. That is the Shaykh’s argument.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00488

Anyone thoughtful can see how weak and incomplete it is. It does not prove that these simple beings love in any real sense; at most, it compares their behaviour to love. Ibn Sina’s account of matter’s love is only an image, not a proof. He has simply replaced other words with words that suit his claim, such as “striving,” “fearing,” and “hurrying.” His claim that matter hurries to exchange one form for another is also false. Matter is something that receives forms; it cannot act. It does not demand or seek anything. It only receives and obeys.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00489

We have already shown, by the method we use to prove that love runs through all beings, that matter is itself a potential for longing and love. It is not something that already longs or loves a particular form. If it did, it would already be an actual form, not matter.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00490

As for Ibn Sina’s account of the form’s love, he says that form strives to remain with its subject, matter, and to remain in its natural place once it reaches it. When it is moved away from that place, it moves back toward it with longing. But this does not prove the point by sound reasoning. It only uses words such as “striving” and “longing,” assuming what it is meant to prove. Simply existing in a subject does not show love for that subject. Nor do stillness in a place after arriving there, or movement back toward it after leaving, prove longing for it. That would require showing that bodily nature is aware of itself and its actions. Ibn Sina did not establish this in that treatise or elsewhere. The same applies to his claim that an accident loves its subject, which he calls obvious even though it is one of the least obvious things. If every necessary relation between two things were love, then every essential property, relation, and connection would love what it belongs to. So would surfaces and boundaries love the bodies whose dimensions they define. That conclusion is plainly false.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00491

Here is an important point. The thinkers who say love runs through all beings mean that each thing loves and longs for what it is, or for its own perfection. It does not love what is lower or less complete than itself, except indirectly. So Ibn Sina’s claim that form loves the matter that supports it is wrong.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00492

Whenever a nature, soul, or power acts, it does not first seek the action it performs or the things it acts on. It seeks something greater: its goal, or its own full perfection. Nature does not seek matter for its own sake; it makes matter a means to gain another perfection. Nature is itself a perfection of matter; matter is not a perfection of nature. Nature therefore takes up and shapes matter so that it can reach a higher perfection. In the same way, the soul does not govern the body and create bodily tools because it loves the body or the tools. It does so because it loves itself and longs for its own perfection.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00493

In short, anyone following the mystics’ path must arrange the loves of beings in an order. The love of each lower being leads upward to love of a higher one, until all lead to love of the Necessary Being. Then all things will be seen to love Him and long to meet Him. The higher being must also love the lower one—not to gain something or become more complete, but as a result of its care and generosity toward it. Since nature completes the body, the body loves what completes it: nature. Since the governing soul completes nature, nature loves the soul. The soul is completed by intellect, so it loves intellect. Intellect is completed by God, the Necessary Being, so intellect loves Him. Through Him, the whole is complete. He is all things in their unity. He rejoices in Himself, not in anything else, for there is nothing other than Him that could stand apart as an equal or partner. He is the Mighty, the Overpowering; He rules over His servants, and all things lie within His reach. In His love for Himself, His love for all things is gathered together, just as His knowledge of Himself includes His knowledge of all things. We explained earlier, in the discussion of knowledge, how this can be so without dividing His absolute oneness. All heavenly and earthly bodies are contained within the souls’ longing for themselves and their intellectual perfections.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00494

The souls’ longing for themselves and their perfections is likewise contained within the intellects’ love for their highest source. And the intellects’ love for their highest source is contained within the splendour of the First Light, the fullest good, the greatest beauty, and the highest majesty, for He is the return and final goal of all things.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00495
XVII. Another way to show that love runs through all things
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00496

The early philosophers gave another general argument for this point. They said that just as all beings receive their existence from causes that give it to them, they also receive their perfections from those causes. These causes do not intend to create any particular effects or their perfections, and what is higher does not look down toward what is lower, or toward its perfection. So divine wisdom, care, good ordering, and the world’s fine arrangement require every being to have love within it. Through this love, it holds on to the perfections it has gained and longs to gain them when they are absent. This produces both the order of the whole and the careful arrangement of its parts.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00497

This love must be a lasting feature of every being. If it could leave, another love would be needed to preserve the first love, which was supposed to preserve the being’s perfection while it had it and restore it when it lost it. If that second love could also leave, we would need another love to preserve it, and so on without end. If the second love could not leave, then one of the two loves would serve no purpose. That is impossible. So love must run through all beings and all their parts.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00498

That is their argument. It is sound, but the one we have already offered is stronger, clearer, and gives a fuller account of why it must be so. We have shown that existence is one reality, but differs in how complete it is; that an effect belongs to the same order of reality as its cause; and that the cause completes the effect. We have also shown that existence is good and pleasant. Every being therefore loves itself and its own perfection. But its perfection is completed by its cause. Since its perfection comes from what is its cause and source, the cause—though it does not intend the effect and does not look toward it, being far above it—must love itself and desire its own being. That very being is what perfects and completes the effect. The effect follows from this completeness.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00499

So every effect is preserved through its love for its cause, and every lower being is ordered through its love for what is above it. If there were no such bond between higher and lower, beings could not endure, and the order could not remain so complete. Disorder and corruption would enter it. The world cannot be held together by each being’s love for itself alone. Nor is love for one’s own perfection enough unless that perfection comes through the being of its cause. To love its own completion is therefore also to love the cause that gives it being.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00500

Nothing can preserve itself, just as nothing can bring itself into existence. Otherwise it would have to come before itself. Preservation means that a thing continues to exist. A possible being depends on a cause other than itself not only when it first comes to be, but also to keep existing. A thing does not preserve its own perfection; in fact, the reverse is true. Its perfection is what gives it its being, makes its matter into a particular thing, and defines its kind.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00501

From all this, we learn that the love that preserves each effect is its love for its cause. This means that its existence is linked to and depends on that cause. Through this link—this dependent existence—the effect keeps its identity and continues through the source that gives it being. This is what people mean when they say, “Without the higher being’s love, the lower would vanish.”
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00502

We have also learned that love runs through all beings in the same order as their existence. Just as each stronger level of existence gives rise to a weaker one, down to matter and bodies, each lower love gives rise to a higher love, until it reaches love of the Necessary Being. According to the perfections suited to them, all beings seek the perfection of the One who is perfect through Himself and resemble Him as they gain that perfection. God, whose names are holy, is the final goal of every being and the end of every level. Love and longing bring beings into existence with all the perfections they can have, and keep them in existence. Without love and longing, no event could occur in the bodily world and nothing could come to be in the world of generation and decay.
